Approach

figures follow approach

Equipment

  • XCore 2 implant/instrument tray (Ø16, Ø18 or Ø22)
  • XLIF Corpectomy instrument tray
  • Maxcess 4 access system, articulating arm & disposables
  • XLIF instruments · NVM5 system & disposables
  • Fixation (e.g. Traverse lateral plate, Armada) · Osteocel Pro

Perform the corpectomy per the XLIF Corpectomy surgical technique (doc #9511977 A), then size.

  1. 1

    Sizing

    • Core Ø · core trial selects 16, 18 or 22 mm.
    • Endcap · Use endcap trials to choose length. XLIF endcaps span the ring apophysis; 30–60 mm lengths depending on core Ø. Disc material must be fully evacuated.
    • Height · seat both caliper tips flush on the superior and inferior endplates. Read the defect height under no distraction (top or side scale).
    • Need more room? The XCore 2 distractor distracts but gives no height reading.
  2. 2

    Implant construction

    • Pick the core from the sizing chart: construct height minus the added height of both endcaps (see Implants → Height calculator).
    • Seat the core in the matching loading block, set screw up, spinning sleeve in the grooves.
    • Turn the silver knurled thumbwheel anticlockwise until the pin shows “unlock”. Slide the zero-profile arms fully into the core slots.
    • Thumbwheel clockwise until the pin reaches “lock”. Two-finger grip; stop once it bottoms out.
    • Orient the inserter shaft to the approach image on the block. Drop the core onto the bottom endcap (mating feature up, spikes down).
    • Short endcap lock screw driver + 2 endcap lock screws per endcap. Driver breaks away when tight. Flip the block and repeat; both endcaps oriented the same way.
    • Check engagement: purple teardrop handle clockwise expands, anticlockwise compresses.
    • Pack Osteocel Pro into the core if required (and around it after implantation).
    Note Flower pattern: endcaps attach in up to 12 angles (30° steps) on Ø18/Ø22 cores and 8 angles (45° steps) on Ø16.
  3. 3

    Implant insertion

    Insert the assembled construct compressed into the prepared space.

    Note Spinning sleeve may face up or down, as long as the rounds and/or lordosis of the endcaps face anterior.
  4. 4

    Implant expansion

    • Teardrop handle clockwise to expand; monitor under fluoroscopy.
    • Full expansion: inner-core threads reach the top of the outer-core aperture, and a positive stop is felt.
    • Collapsed space or more control: attach the counter-torque handle.
    Caution Do not keep turning at full compression or full expansion. Over-expanding or over-compressing can strip the implant.
  5. 5

    Inserter release

    Thumbwheel anticlockwise to release, then pull the inserter straight off the core.

  6. 6

    Final tightening

    Confirm final height. Core lock screw driver on the core set screw, clockwise until it breaks away at 10 in-lb.

  7. 7

    Fixation

    Select and place the chosen fixation, e.g. Traverse lateral plate.

  8. 8

    Construct removal

    Unlock the core set screw with the set screw driver: about a half turn anticlockwise.

    Note A half turn is enough. Backed out too far, the set screw can stop the inserter re-engaging.
  9. 9

    Retract the core

    • Thumbwheel fully anticlockwise (check the unlock indicator).
    • Slide the arms into the core slots so the inserter engages the set-screw face.
    • Thumbwheel clockwise to lock; teardrop handle anticlockwise to collapse; remove carefully.

Spikes add a further 2 mm. The caliper scale already accounts for endcaps and spikes.

Construct

Exploded construct. Endcap slides onto the core and locks with an endcap set screw; the core locks with the core set screw. Large central and anterior graft windows.
Archon reconstruction plate · supplemental fixation. Third screw point at each end, 13 mm between fixation points, 20 mm wide.

Equipment & monitoring

  • XCore Mini instruments and implants
  • NVM5: free-run EMG (RLN via EMG ET tube), MEP and SSEP cord monitoring

Shown for an anterior approach; the posterior thoracic (costotransversectomy) sequence is identical.

  1. 1

    Corpectomy

    Anterior corpectomy at the target level(s) by standard technique. For a posterior thoracic approach, a costotransversectomy reaches the anterior column.

    Note Confirm cord integrity with MEPs after the corpectomy. NVM5 EMG ET tube monitors the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
    Caution Do not breach the subchondral bone when preparing endplates; it raises the risk of subsidence and vertebral body fracture.
  2. 2

    Core sizing

    • Core sizer first: Ø12 or Ø14 mm.
    • Caliper next: read the grid for the construct type (parallel, lordotic or hybrid).
    • Check the height matches the segment height from pre-op planning.
  3. 2a

    Reading the caliper

    The coloured bars on the caliper point to the core, e.g. red = 22–34 mm core. Pick the core for the chosen diameter and height.

    Note The caliper already allows for endcaps and spikes, so no extra maths is needed. For reference: parallel endcaps add 1.5 mm, contoured/lordotic/kyphotic 2.5 mm, spikes 2 mm.
  4. 3

    Endplate sizing

    Endplate sizer on both the superior and inferior endplates. Choose the footprint and shape with the most endplate coverage to limit subsidence.

  5. 4

    Construct assembly

    • Knurled knob fully anticlockwise. Mate the expansion barrel driver with the coloured spinning wheel, then knob clockwise to lock.
    • Slide endcaps on following the lasermarked arrow (anterior). Match T and B endcaps to the core marks.
    • Place endcap set screws; final-tighten with the final tightening handle.
    Note Two-finger grip. Once the indicator pin passes the vertical line the inserter locks as soon as resistance is felt.
  6. 5

    Insert the construct

    Insert the assembled construct into the prepared space. The core can go right side up or upside down.

  7. 6

    Expand the construct

    • Black knob to expand; positive stop at full expansion.
    • 1 turn = 0.5 mm; 10 turns = 5 mm.
    • Expand close to final height before graft packing.
    • Take the final x-ray with the inserter still attached.
    Caution Avoid over-distraction. Use radiographic confirmation and neuromonitoring; C5 root is at particular risk. Restored height should match pre-op planning.
  8. 7

    Release the inserter

    Silver knurled knob anticlockwise, then pull the inserter straight off.

  9. 8

    Final tightening

    Screw driver with breakaway final tightening handle on the core set screw, clockwise until it clicks off at 10 in-lb. One click = locked.

    Note Place supplemental fixation (e.g. Archon plate) at the necessary levels. Confirm cord integrity with MEPs after the construct.
  10. R1

    Removal · loosen set screw

    Set screw driver, half turn anticlockwise only.

    Note Backed out too far, the set screw blocks the inserter from re-engaging.
  11. R2

    Removal · retract & remove

    Knob fully anticlockwise, re-engage the spinning wheel, knob clockwise to lock. Black handle anticlockwise until fully collapsed; remove and unload on the back table.

Source discrepancies to check
  • Mini Ø14 core 5964152 printed “15–12 mm” in the catalogue (shown as 15–20).
  • Mini endcap table lists 5962741 (T) for Ø14 contoured 17×14; the catalogue gives 5964741 (used here).
  • Mini 5964961 (Ø14 contoured 19×16) appears in the endcap table but not the catalogue.
  • XCore 2 Ø16 43–75 core: catalogue 7160075 / 43–75; sizing chart shows 44–75 and 7180067 for 37–63.
  • XCore 2 Ø16 XLIF 16×30 4° listed as 5164004; no 16×40 4° in the catalogue.
  • XCore 2 Ø18 core trial is catalogued as “endcap trail, Ø18 mm” (7181001). No Ø22 core trial listed.
